articleTitle: Adaptive Inertia VSG Control Method Involving Power and Power Change Rate
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: By simulating the inertia and damping characteristics of the synchronous generator, the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control enables the inverters to provide inertia and damping support for the system, which can effectively improve the frequency stability of the high-scale new energy power system. However, in this control strategy, if the inertia link is set too small, it has no significant effect on the frequency change. If the inertia is set too large, it will lead to system oscillation. Fixed inertia coefficients in traditional VSG control can’t meet the requirements of stable operation of inverters under different working conditions. For this reason, an adaptive inertia VSG control method with power and power change rate is proposed, which limits the frequency change rate of inverters to a certain range and improves the stability of self-organizing power grid. Finally, the effectiveness of this control method is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Unleashing the Potential of Digital Twin Technology in Microgrid – A Case Study of a Tropical Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Digital twinning concept is applied in various industry areas in the wave of information and communication technology advancement. A digital replica of a microgrid is referred to as microgrid digital twin which can provide massive enhancement to microgrid design, planning, optimization, forecasting, system reliability analysis, etc. a microgrid digital twin models the physical dynamics of real assets and with a real-time simulation and feed-through of data from real world sensors and meters. Microgrid digital twin can fulfill the purpose of creating a digital test bed with high fidelity that can be used in both academic and industry parties with lower cost, faster product development cycles and minimum electrical hazards. In this paper, an experimental microgrid in Singapore is selected as the real twin and a digital twin is created. The digital twin is built using a hardware-controller-in-the-loop real-time simulation (HCILRTS) design. The development and validation process of the digital twin is shared in this paper. More importantly, a conceptual exploration of different potential applications of microgrid digital twin is shared considering the up-to-date technology.

articleTitle: Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Prediction Based on Bayesian Regularized BP Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In view of the problem that the randomness and volatility of photovoltaic power generation lead to low prediction accuracy, this paper proposes a short-term prediction method for photovoltaic power generation power based on Bayesian regularization algorithm to optimize BP neural network, and analyzes the factors affecting photovoltaic power generation power prediction model for photovoltaic power generation was established, which was trained in neural networks by Bayesian regularization algorithm optimization, L-M optimization algorithm and traditional gradient drop method, and the prediction results of the three methods were compared with the study, and the experimental results showed that the method proposed in this paper was effective Improved photovoltaic power prediction accuracy, which can be used for short-term accurate prediction of photovoltaic power.

articleTitle: Carbon Footprint Analysis of 220kV Flame Retardant XLPE Insulated Power Cables
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Power cables and other power equipment are significant sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in power transmission networks. To achieve the goals of carbon reduction and carbon neutrality, it is crucial to promote the decarbonization of power grids and equipment. Therefore, it is necessary to establish a calculation method for the carbon footprint of power cables from a life cycle assessment (LCA) perspective. This will enable the formulation of a carbon emission management strategy to guide the reduction of carbon emissions associated with power cables. This paper proposed a whole life cycle carbon footprint calculation model. As a case study, the carbon footprint of a 220kV flame retardant XLPE insulated power cable was analyzed. The result revealed that the cable's carbon footprint is primarily attributed to the operation phase (95.4%), followed by the carbon footprint associated with raw materials. Potential solutions for reducing carbon emissions were also discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization of Cogging Torque of Permanent Magnet-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor Based on Improved Taguchi Method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: To improve the performance of permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance motors for wind power generation during operation and reduce cogging torque, an improved iterative Taguchi optimization algorithm was used to perform multi-objective optimization for permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance motors. Taking slot width, air gap length, permanent magnet thickness, and magnetic isolation bridge width as optimization variables, the electromagnetic torque, cogging torque, and efficiency are analyzed using the optimal factor combination obtained by orthogonal test methods. Ansoft Maxwell verifies the optimal combination, and the optimal combination of the optimal factors with the lowest cogging torque is preferred. The simulation results show that the improved iterative Taguchi method significantly reduces the cogging torque of the motor, significantly improves efficiency compared to before optimization, and effectively improves the motor’s operating performance. The improved Taguchi method improves the calculation accuracy based on the traditional Taguchi method and is more suitable for practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: A Dual-Loop Control Strategy Based on PI and Repetitive Control for APF with CoolSiC™ MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) can effectively suppress current distortion and voltage fluctuation in the grid. Due to the fact that the reference current tracking signal of the APF is an AC signal that is superimposed with multiple harmonic currents, high demands are required for the control strategy. In addition, the switching frequency of IGBT is limited by its intrinsic characteristics and heat dissipation capacity, typically resulting in a frequency lower than 20kHz. Therefore, the compensation performance is constrained. In this regard, this article proposes a dual-loop composite control strategy based on PI and repetitive control (PIRC) for an APF prototype which is designed based on the latest CoolSiC™ MOSFET device. Extracting harmonic currents and designing a decoupling control system in the single synchronous rotating coordinate system, and using a switching frequency of 40kHz for the MOSFETs. The simulation and prototype experimental results demonstrate that the proposed control strategy applied in the developed APF prototype has a high compensation performance.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Environment under Switching Operation in Different High-Voltage Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The localized intelligent secondary equipment arranged in the substation is often directly installed near the high voltage side. And high-voltage substations’ secondary side gathered large amount of localized electronic equipment. In the gas insulated switchgear (GIS) substation environment, the electromagnetic interference (EMI) at certain moments will exceeds the threshold specified in standards. This work tests transient and steady-state EMI in high-voltage substation of different voltage rate. And revealed the harsh EMI at the secondary side of substation will affect the electromagnetic immunity of the localized secondary electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Under Seawater Capacitive Power Transfer for Maritime Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Underwater capacitive power transfer (CPT) can provide an inexpensive and light electric charging solution with good misalignment tolerance for unmanned maritime vehicles. This paper investigates the effect of the changing of the frequency and the distance on the power transfer and overall efficiency of the underwater CPT system, considering the dielectric losses of the medium. It also proposes and validates a mathematical model for calculating the maximum available efficiency of the system. Using series compensations, the proposed CPT can transfer 48 W at 500 mm, 48 V input voltage, 516 kHz, and 54%.

articleTitle: Gravity Battery: A New Innovation for a Sustainable Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Despite the fact that renewable energy resources play a significant role in dealing with the global warming and in achieving carbon neutrality, they cannot be effectively used until they combine with a suitable energy storage technology. Gravity batteries are viewed as promising and sustainable energy storage, they are clean, free, easy accessible, high efficiency, and long lifetime. There are six technologies of gravity battery: Gravitricity, Mountain Gravity Energy Storage (MGES), Energy Vault, Marlon’s Energy Storage Blog, Sink Float Soltuion, and Advanced Rail Energy Storage. The current papers aims at presenting the different gravity batteries technologies and comparing between them in terms of LCOS, advantages, drawbacks, power rating, life time and efficiency. Results showed that the common advantages of the presented technologies of gravity batteries are the scalability, high efficiency, long lifetime that can reach 50 years, fast ramp up, and low LCOS with a range of 50$/MWh for gravitricity and 770 $/MWh for the technology Sink Float solution with wind turbine. Moreover, the gravitricity has the highest efficiency, for energy storage that can reach 90%, and the longest lifetime (up to 50 years). The cheapest technology is the MGES. The main disadvantages are the short term storage, and the availability of data for the methods that use the abandoned mines.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Cooling Characteristics of Hybrid Liquid Spray and Air Cooling for an EV Battery Pack
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In an electric vehicle, battery thermal management system plays a critical role in the maintaining optimal temperatures inside the battery pack to extend its lifespan, improve its performance along with the operational safety. Several attempts have been made to achieve the practical and efficient systems of battery thermal management. The contribution of previous research on this topic has received little attention on the evaporative cooling to dissipate excess heat from the battery pack during charging and discharge cycles. This study focuses on investigating the cooling performance of a battery thermal management system in an electric vehicle that uses forced-air cooling along with a non-electrically conductive liquid spray. The liquid spray used in the simulation was the hydrofluoroether (HFE) Novec-7100 fluid developed by 3M. The study consisted of simulations that evaluated the impact of the fluid injection rate on the heat removal performance of a 40-cell cylindrical lithium-ion battery pack. The results showed that using the HFE liquid spray was effective in reducing the maximum temperature and improving the temperature uniformity compared to using only air cooling. However, the cooling performance weakened as the flow rate of HFE increased. The optimal flow rate of HFE should be determined for effective thermal management of the densely-packed batteries.

articleTitle: Power Decoupling Control of Grid-Forming Converter Based on Voltage and Angle Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Grid-forming (GFM) converters are widely used because of its great performances of grid-connected. However, the coupling between active power and reactive power makes hard to realize independent control of active power and reactive power. The power coupling has adverse effects on control performance, such as synchronization instability and power oscillations. In order to solve the issue of the power coupling, the paper analyses the nature of power coupling with a virtual synchronous generator (VSG) grid-connected system. A power decoupling control is proposed based on the relationship between active power and reactive power. The voltage compensation and the angle compensation are employed in the power loop to reduce the power cross-coupling. Finally, by comparing with traditional VSG, the simulation results verify the effectiveness of proposed decoupling control in the paper.

articleTitle: Coupling Simulation Analysis of Electromagnetic, Vibration and Noise Multi-physical Fields for Dry-type Core Reactor
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Iron core reactors are widely used to compensate for capacitance current in substations. Due to electromagnetic force and magnetostrictive effect, vibration and noise problems of the reactors are very serious. In this paper, an iron core reactor model is established based on the multiphysical field finite element method. Through the simulation calculation, the characteristics and mechanism of reactor vibration and radiation noise are analyzed. In addition, the influence of core structure on vibration and noise is analyzed through the simulation of core vibration mode and natural frequency. The research results can provide a theoretical basis for iron core reactor vibration and noise reduction.

articleTitle: Digital Technology for New-Type Power Systems in the Context of "Dual Carbon"
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: To achieve the "dual carbon" goal, energy is the main battlefield, and electricity is the main force. In order to contribute to the "dual carbon" goal, China is actively building a new-type power system, promoting digital transformation, and ensuring national energy security and sustainable development strategy. This paper first expounds the necessity of building a new-type power system and reviews the enabling direction of digital technology. Then the new-type power system is summarized, the connotation and development requirements of the new-type power system are summarized, and its development status is briefly expounded. Finally, based on the needs of the development of new-type power systems, the common digital technologies of new-type power system development are sorted out. This paper covers the current status, development needs and application prospects of new-type power system digital technology, which can provide some reference for the current research and power system development around new-type power system digital technology.

articleTitle: Grid-Tied Inverter Fractional-Order Phase Compensation via Odd Repetition Control
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Proportional Integral Multi-Resonant Conventional Repetitive (PIMR-CRC) has good fundamental signal tracking, harmonic signal suppression ability, and excellent dynamic performance. The current harmonics of the single-phase grid-tied inverter system are mainly odd, so the proportional-integral multi-resonant odd repetitive control (PIMR-ORC) based on odd repetitive control is proposed. However, the phase lead compensation accuracy affects the harmonic suppression performance of the PIMR-ORC system. For this reason, a new fractional compensated PIMR-ORC (FO-PIMR-ORC) strategy based on the Thiran IIR filter is proposed. First, the stability of the PIMR-ORC control system is analyzed. Then the implementation of fractional-order phase lead compensation based on the IIR filter and the stability analysis of the FO-PIMR-ORC are given. Taking the single-phase LCL grid-tied inverter as an example, the parameter design of FO-PIMR-ORC is given. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed control strategy is verified by MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Vertical Axis Wind Turbine Powers Telecom Towers: Green and Clean Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This study proposes an application of vertical-axis wind turbines to power telecom towers in off-grid areas. Telecom services play a critical role in a country, and the majority of the people use their services in daily life. Moreover, this network is growing. Despite this development, it is essential to decarbonize the telecom power supply. Literature suggests replacing telecom towers' traditional fossil fuel energy with sustainable energy such as solar and wind resources. According to countries' investment and interest, wind energy currently has the fastest energy resource development. Since there are many off-grid telecom towers, using the wind turbine is an excellent choice. However, it must be considered which type and wind turbine(s) installation is appropriate, economical, and low-maintenance costs. Small-scale vertical-axis wind turbines are one of the best options among available resources; with this suggestion, they can be installed on the telecom tower, which has extensive economic and technical advantages. Furthermore, the hybrid power supply of vertical-axis wind turbines and fuel cells makes the telecom tower supply fully green and clean.

articleTitle: Grid Frequency Composite Support Strategy for Voltage Source Converter-Synchronous Generator Paralleled System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: For strengthening the frequency stability of a power system dominated by new energy, a grid frequency composite support strategy for a converter-synchronous generator paralleled system is proposed. The traditional droop control with a low-pass filter can provide inertia for the power grid, but the power output must be along with the power droop curve, which weakens the high dynamic performance of the inverter. Therefore, in this paper, the equivalent load disturbance component is introduced into the droop control loop, and the reference frequency generated from the active-frequency loop is corrected to enhance the short-term support capability of the active power. In the paralleled system of inverter and conventional synchronous generator, the power grid composite support of short-term and long-term provided by inverter and synchronous generator is achieved by the proposed method, respectively. The 2-norm and infinite norm are used as the evaluation indexes for the proposed controller parameters, which are optimized by the particle swarm optimization algorithm, and the optimal frequency composite support is achieved for the converter-synchronous generator paralleled system.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Partial Shading Losses in Photovoltaic Systems with Power Optimisers
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Partial Shading effect due to clouds cover in tropics has a great influence on PV efficiency and the generated power reliability. This work showcases the potential of using photovoltaic power optimisers (PVPO) to mitigate the impact of partial shading in string inverter PV systems. The simulation of the characteristics of the PV system under partial shading conditions will be correlated to an actual agrivolatic farm which has been setup for analysis. The findings will provide a clearer understanding on the use of Module Level Power Electronics (MLPE) to mitigate power losses due to array mismatch caused by partial shading and aging of the PV modules.

articleTitle: Optimization Complimentary Planning with Energy Storage in Multi-energy System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Multi-energy complementary microgrid systems can take advantage of the characteristics of various types of energy sources, improve energy utilization efficiency, increase economic benefits, reduce the cost of electricity, and reduce carbon emissions. This work takes new multi-energy complementary microgrid system as an example. The multi-energy complementary microgrid systems model including wind power, photovoltaic, electrochemical battery storage system, gas generator set. This work takes industrial project in Pakistan as a practical case. And maximizing the benefits at the lowest cost as the optimization goal, the multi-energy complementary microgrid system is modeled and simulated during the whole life cycle of the project. The optimal capacity ratio of various types of energy is obtained according to the calculation results, which can provide reference for similar projects.

articleTitle: Torque and Speed Regulation Characteristic Analysis of Axial Permanent Magnet Coupler
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: As a non-contact magnetic transmission device, the analysis of its transmission torque, especially the maximum torque and starting torque, is very important for the load capacity and starting capacity of the magnetic coupler. In this paper, taking an axial permanent magnet asynchronous magnetic coupler as an example, the effects of changing the thickness and conductivity of the copper disc on the maximum torque, starting torque, and variable load speed regulation characteristics of the magnetic coupler are analyzed by the calculation formula of the transmission torque. Then, a three-dimensional finite element model of the magnetic coupler is established by the finite element simulation software, and the analysis results of the above analytical method are verified by the finite element simulation results, which provides a reference direction for the early design and optimization of the magnetic coupler. The results show that the output speed is abrupt when air gap thickness is between g = 15 and 17 mm; the speed regulation range is small between g = 3 and 15 mm, whereas the speed regulation effect is good between g = 15 and 30 mm.

articleTitle: Optimal Secondary and Tertiary Hierarchical Control for Photovoltaic System Generation Using a Heuristic Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This paper proposes a secondary and tertiary optimal methodology to control an electrical distribution system with photovoltaic generation. The control is hierarchical, and the optimization relies on heuristics; thus, the optimal approach minimizes the error, comparing the output with the reference, but the methodology maintains an acceptable operational cost. The objective function determines the optimal controller’s coefficient to improve system performance. The steady-state response does not have an overshoot, and it is over-damped. Considering the presence of non-linear elements, the response time is sufficiently fast. Moreover, despite the increase in load, the settling time is less than 0.4 seconds, and the system output satisfies the system requirements in terms of power and voltage.

articleTitle: Green GDP Accounting Model Based on Material Flow Analysis and BP Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: GDP is an important accounting indicator of national economy, but GDP is difficult to measure the environmental pollution expenditure of a country or a region, which cuts the relationship between economic development and sustainable development and is not in line with the concept of global green and sustainable development. This paper proposes two models for calculating GGDP, one is the CPMF model based on material flow analysis, which achieves the quantification of statistics by monetizing the amount of environmental inputs and environmental outputs; the other is the GGDP accounting model based on BP neural network, which takes environmental pollution expenditure as the input layer and GGDP as the output layer variable to form an accounting model. The two models calculated GGDP as follows: in 2000, the calculated value of GGDP was $9.43×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> (CPMF model) and $1.03×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> (BP neural network), while it grew to $1.86×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> (CPMF model) and $1.69×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> (BP neural network) in 2018. In order to provide the government with directions for environmental management, this paper uses gray correlation analysis and coefficient of variation method, and the highly correlated (high weight) variables of environmental pollution expenditure and GGDP are the amount of investment in environmental pollution control and total natural gas consumption.

articleTitle: Short-Term Electricity Load Forecasting Based on Back Propagation Neural Network Considering Key Meteorological Factors
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Power load forecasting has an important impact on the safe dispatch of the electric grid and the operation of the national economy. A method based on the back propagation neural network was proposed and considered the key meteorological factor to improve the accuracy of electricity load forecasting. Firstly, this paper analyzed the influence of different meteorological factors on electricity load. Secondly, key meteorological factors and historical electricity loads were used as input vectors to the temporal convolutional network for electricity load forecasting. The results showed that considering meteorological factor could effectively improve the accuracy of load forecasting.

articleTitle: Ensemble Boosting Method of Power System Transient Stability Assessment Based on Cost-Sensitive Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Data-driven techniques have proven effective in enhancing prediction accuracy and speed for power system transient stability assessment (TSA). However, these methods are still beset by challenges such as small sample size issues and lack of interpretability. To address these problems, this study proposes a transient power system evaluation method based on Adacost, which uses a neural network as the base classifier and introduces a cost-sensitive coefficient into the Adaboost algorithm to increase the adjustment coefficient of misclassified samples. The proposed model is validated on an electromechanical transient simulation example of the IEEE39 bus test system, demonstrating its efficiency in handling cases with imbalanced sample categories. Furthermore, the SHAP method are employed to explain the model prediction results in terms of feature importance.

articleTitle: A Carbon Hub Matrix Model Considering Carbon Emission Flow Loss of Energy Hub
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: As the core component of the integrated energy system (IES), the energy station (EH) plays a role in the conversion and distribution of various energy sources. The existing research on the EH internal carbon emission flow (CEF) has ignored the EH carbon flow loss. Based on constructing carbon flow models for different types of energy converters, a carbon hub model considering EH carbon flow loss is proposed for the first time, and its standard matrix form is given to describe the EH port carbon potential relationship and the internal CEF conversion and distribution process. Finally, an actual EH is selected for analysis, and the relationship and characteristics of the internal and external CEF of the EH under the consideration of carbon loss are given. In addition, two kinds of renewable energy, centralized photovoltaics (PV) and hydrogen enriched compressed natural gas (HCNG), are introduced into the EH to compare with the initial case, to analyze the operation rules of carbon hubs in the scenario of renewable energy penetration.

articleTitle: Active Damping Control Strategy for Bus Voltage of Special Vehicle Based on Virtual Resistance
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In the power system of special vehicles, the proportion of constant power load Constant Power Load (CPL) increases, and its negative impedance characteristics cause the oscillation of bus voltage, this paper proposes a virtual resistor active damping control strategy based on droop control. Firstly, the equivalent model of the structure of DC microgrid and the equivalent model of CPL are analyzed, and then a virtual resistance strategy suitable for Boost converter is proposed. In addition, a nonlinear disturbance observer (NDO) is designed to achieve fast tracking of disturbances in the system without adding additional current sensors, and the nonlinear disturbance observer is used to get rid of the strong dependence of the control algorithm on the output current sensor. The combination of NDO and virtual resistance control improves the load compensation capability of the control strategy and eliminates the voltage deviation caused by droop control through voltage compensation. Finally, use MATLAB /Simulink to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on Harmonic Suppression of OW-PMSM with Common DC Bus for Three-parameter Digital Notch Filter Based on Voltage Compensation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In order to suppress the 5th, 7th, 11th and 13th harmonics in the Open-Winding Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (OW-PMSM) with common DC bus, a novel harmonic extraction strategy is studied in this paper. The three-parameter notch filter (TPNF) is used to extract the harmonic current, and the voltage is compensated by feedforward compensation. The stability of the OW-PMSM with common DC bus based on 120° decoupled modulation with the TPNF is discussed. Finally, the simulation results show that the TPNF researched in this paper directly uses the notch center, the actual amplitude and width as the notch parameters. The coupling relationship between the notch filter factors not only be solved, but also the 5th, 7th, 11th and 13th harmonics of the motor current can be effectively suppressed. The torque ripple which caused by harmonics is reduced, and the control precision of OW-PMSM system is improved.

articleTitle: Research on Ion Current Density Measurement under HVDC Transmission Line Based on Inversion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: To maintain the normal and stable operation of high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission facilities and ensure the quality of HVDC electromagnetic environment, the measurement results of the electric field and the ion current density under the HVDC transmission line need attention. A simple measurement method can reduce the workload of operation and maintenance personnel. However, the ion current density measuring device and electric field measuring device are still two independent devices, which is not convenient enough. In this study, an inversion algorithm is presented to establish the relationship between electric field and ion current density. Then the ground-level ion current density can be obtained directly based on the measurement results of the electric field, which can simplify the measurement process. First, an ion flow field inversion model is established. Second, an example is used to compare the generalized inversion method and the regularization inversion method, which shows that the regularization inversion method is more accurate. Hence, it is selected to participate in subsequent calculations. Third, the inversion results are discussed and compared with the measurement results. Finally, the electric field on the wire and ground-level ion current density, which is calculated at different areas of the used conductor using the inversion algorithm, are studied. It is found that the results of the inversion algorithm are in good agreement with the measurement results of the Wilson plate, and this work provides a new idea for ion current density measurement.

articleTitle: Distributed Solution for Pareto Front Based Multi-objective OPF
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Pareto front (PF) based multi-objective OPF (MO-OPF) is an effective tool in power system operation and an efficient multi-objective algorithm is necessary to tackle it. In addition, under some scenarios this algorithm needs to have distributed solution capability to cope with some difficulties in operation. Most of the existing distributed MO-OPF approaches are based on mathematical programming techniques by which a multi-objective problem needs to be converted into multiple single-objective problems (SOP). The tedious repetition of algorithmic executions is inevitable. In this study, coevolutionary algorithm (CA) is applied to solve the distributed MO-OPF. The problem is decomposed based on decision variables. After segmenting by the geographical division, multiple subpopulations are coevolved among areas and a distributed power flow calculation method is embedded to support the distributed fitness evaluation. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the distributed approach and the advantages of the second decomposition.

articleTitle: Optimization Analysis of Electromagnetic Structure of Traction Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The traction motor has the characteristics of high power density, large volume and high efficiency. In recent years, it has been widely used in transportation, aerospace equipment and industrial fields. This paper takes 1150 kW traction motor as the research object. The length, thickness and stator outer diameter of the permanent magnet of the motor are selected as the optimization objects. The rated torque, rated point efficiency and rated power are the optimization objectives. The global response surface optimization algorithm is used to optimize the motor structure.

articleTitle: Explore the Effect of Different Parameters on Eliminating the Snapback of RC-IGBT with P-poly Trench-Collectors
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: RC-IGBTs. As a semiconductor device of great significance in the fields of power transmission, industry, national defense and medical care, the research of IGBT has been one of the hot spots in power electronics research and has made important contributions to promote the green energy revolution. At present, the emergence of RC-IGBT effectively solves the problems of parasitic inductance and high cost caused by the traditional parallel diode IGBTs, but the new problem is the short-circuit effect of n-collector, when the collector is injected into the hole will produce a back-absorption effect, resulting in wasted energy consumption. To achieve higher energy efficiency, this paper presents an RC-IGBT with two p-poly trench collectors that have high resistance in the forward state to suppress the back-jump effect and low resistance in the reverse state to conduct the anti-parallel diode. An 8 µm width model was explored to ensure the elimination of back-hopping and lower resistance values to reduce energy consumption. The results show that the optimal trench width and doping concentration are 4 µm and 1e20 cm^-3, respectively, leading to the conclusion that the model is applicable to all RC-IGBTs.

articleTitle: Sliding-Mode Control of PMSM Speed Loop Based on Adaptive Power Reaching Law
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of poor dynamic control and large chattering in the speed control system of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM), a sliding-mode control strategy based on adaptive power reaching law is developed in this paper. First, the motion of the system state at different stages under the action of the traditional power-reaching aw is analyzed. Second, a new reaching law is designed using the mapping relationship of functions, and the reaching law parameters can be dynamically adjusted according to the system state. Then, the reaching law is used to design the velocity loop sliding-mode controller and perform the Lyapunov stability analysis. Finally, the motor speed is controlled by an adaptive power-law speed-loop sliding-mode controller with Simulink software and compared with a conventional power-law reaching-law controller. The results show that the new controller designed in this paper reduces the speed overshoot after starting the motor, enhances the dynamic response of the system and effectively weakens the sliding-mode chattering, and has good dynamic and static performance.

articleTitle: Equivalent Wind Farm Model Considering Different Wind Speeds and Wake Effects
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The traditional detailed model of wind farms is unsuitable for large wind farms due to the complexity, long simulation time and high hardware requirements. This paper presents an equivalent model for large wind farms, and the effects of different wind speeds and wake effects are considered. Wind turbine generators (WTGs) with the same wind speed were classified and equivalent models of each part of WTG was established. An equivalent model for WTGs was established for different wind speeds and wake effects based on multimachine equivalence method. The simulation results show that under the same hardware configuration and software step size, the required simulation time of the equivalent wind farm model is reduced significantly with good accuracy.

articleTitle: Identification of Weak Branches in Power System Based on Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: With the inevitable trend of grid-connected operation of a high proportion of new energy sources in new generation power system, the actual operation of power systems is highly stochastic and uncertain. Under such circumstances, traditional methods for identifying weak branches in power systems are difficult to be applied in actual operation due to the problems of calculation speed and calculation accuracy, which promote the application of data-driven methods for weak branch identification in power systems. In this paper, a decision tree based method for weak branch identification is proposed, which takes into account the algorithm interpretability, and simulations are conducted in the IEEE39 system to authenticate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: System Strength Evaluation of a Multi-terminal Power Grid Integrated a Distributed PV Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: With the increasing deployment of renewable energy generations (REGs) for utility and home business scales, the technical constrains and design considerations are becoming more critical. The design of REG systems must be not relied only on the local specifications and load profiles, but also the characteristics of the connected power grids. For example, the power grid impedance characteristics has a significant impact on the capability, stability and quality of the integrated REG. For photovoltaic (PV) systems, this impact becomes more considerable with power penetration and the bulky use of EMI and interface inductive filters. Therefore, this paper seeks the grid impacts on the designing of grid-connected PV systems. The short circuit ratio (SCR) and the maximum transmitted power are defined to obtain the capability of the PV interfaced inverters, with maintaining the voltage stability at the point of common coupling (PCC). In addition, the grid power flow is evaluated under different grid designs. The four terminals power system was discussed in this study to investigate the most common topology used for low voltage (LV) distribution networks and the modern micro grids. The analysis effectiveness in this paper is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Control Strategy of Five-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Multiphase permanent magnet synchronous generator is a potential generator type gradually adopted in renewable energy power generation system. This paper takes five phase permanent magnet synchronous generator as the research object, to build a mathematical model of the power generation system, including the topology structure of AC/DC rectifier and the boost circuit structure, and analyzes the three open circuit fault types of the power generation system. And then taking the minimum copper loss of the stator as the constraint condition, this paper has completed the analysis and calculation of the compensation current vector of the open winding five phase permanent magnet synchronous generator control system under several common open circuit faults. At the same time, aiming at the problem that the algorithm is more complex due to the variety of faults, a unified expression form of current compensation strategy is proposed. The simulation results show that the fault tolerant control strategy for single phase, adjacent two phase and non-adjacent two-phase open circuit faults is feasible under the condition of minimum stator copper loss constraint.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Broadband Oscillation Monitoring Based on Windowed Interpolation and ZoomFFT
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for detecting broadband oscillations in modern power systems, based on the combination of Windowed Interpolation FFT (WIFFT) and ZoomFFT algorithms. The WIFFT method chooses the Blackman-Harris window and three-spectral line interpolation to achieve high accuracy and reduced spectral leakage and interference from white noise. Simulation signals are used to evaluate the performance of the proposed method, and the results demonstrate its high accuracy and applicability in the detection of multimodal broadband oscillations.

articleTitle: In-Situ State of Health Analysis and Simulation of Electric Vehicle Battery Packs Using Conventional Charging Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The authors propose and compare two in-situ methods for the state of health estimation of an electric vehicle battery pack, without the requirement of dismantling the battery from the vehicle. Using the conventional charging infrastructure, the authors achieved a reproducible and comparable testing environment that allows cost efficient state of health observation over the vehicles life time. Pulse and constant current testing methods have been used to identify the internal resistance, available capacity and open circuit voltage of the battery. The obtained data were implemented into a RINT battery simulation model for verification purposes. The simulation was performed to verify the data sets obtained using the two different methods against data from real world drives, as well as to compare the two against each other. Comparison of the simulation model results against 30 unique real world drives has shown, that the state of health defining parameters "internal resistance" and "available capacity" have been properly estimated using the two methods and that usability could be verified. In comparison against each other, the pulse charge testing has shown to provide better results than the constant current testing, while also requiring less time to perform the test. A detailed explanation of the used methods is given in the full paper.

articleTitle: Thermodynamic and Exergoeconomic Analysis of Utilizing a Modified Kalina Cycle for a Recompression Supercritical CO2 Cycle Waste Heat Recovery
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This research introduces a new combined cycle system, coupling supercritical CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (sCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) with a modified Kalina cycle (MKC). By replacing the traditional throttle valve with an expander between the separator and regenerator of this latter unit, expansion work is recaptured that had previously been lost during throttling processes. An exergoeconomic comparison between the combined sCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/MKC and singularly operating sCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> cycle has been conducted to determine how specific decision variables affect system performance. To do so, researchers developed a parametric analysis based on a self-developed thermodynamic simulation platform using Engineering Equation Solver (EES) software. Our results demonstrate that maximizing system performance is achieved through a positive balance between the main compressor pressure ratio (RP), and evaporating pressure (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EV</inf>). Moreover, obtaining lower pinch points between evaporation temperatures along with higher ammonia water masses appears to yield desirable outcomes. Our findings demonstrate that the sCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/MKC offers enhanced exergy efficiency, with an advantage of up to 12.8% over its sCO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> cycle counterpart. This is accompanied by a reduction in total product cost for the former, with savings reaching 6.7%.

articleTitle: Concept for a Stepwise Approach for an Automated Verification Process of Balancing Services
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: To ensure system stability in the power grid, transmission system operators (TSO) are responsible for balancing grid frequency fluctuations by means of balancing services. In many cases, balancing service providers (BSP) aggregate several technical units for the provision of balancing energy. However, beyond the compensation process for the BSP, no monitoring process for the proper provision of required balancing energy by the TSOs exists so far. This paper presents a stepwise concept for a verification process in which the most relevant monitoring requirements of the TSOs are met. These include the exclusive participation of pre-qualified technical units in the balancing service, as well as the correct forwarding of the requested balancing energy from the BSP to its technical units and their proper provision within a tolerated range. The presented concept enables the tamper-resistant storage and retrieval of the required data for verification. In the second stage of the concept, the utilization of a Zero-Knowledge Proof additionally ensures that the verification is performed automatically and in compliance with the BSP’s trade secrets. The integration of the monitoring of individual units creates additional value since filtering for faulty units is made possible for both the TSO and the BSP. For a possible implementation of the concept, we discuss and evaluate the usage of the technologies blockchain and public key infrastructure.

articleTitle: Compression of Power Quality Disturbance Using Wavelet-Atomic Decomposition for Grid-Connected Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The intermittency, volatility, and randomness of the power output of wind farms lead to serious power quality problems at the point of common coupling (PCC) of wind farms. Many waveform recording signals have high requirements for data transmission and storage, which is not conducive to wind power disturbance data analysis. Therefore, a power quality disturbance data compression method based on integrated wavelet and atomic decomposition is proposed to improve the compression ratio and computational complexity. According to the characteristics of power quality disturbance signal, a small-scale coherent atomic dictionary was established to characterize the disturbance components. Based on the small-scale atomic dictionary, the main components of the signal are represented in parametric atomics by atomic decomposition with the matching pursuit algorithm to achieve data compression. Then the irregular residuals of the signal are further decomposed by wavelet method to improve the effectiveness. Simulation results indicates that the proposed method inherits the high compression ratio of atomic decomposition, and further reduces the computational complexity of residual signal decomposition by wavelet transform, obtaining high compression ratios along with high signal-to-noise ratios.

articleTitle: Study of Noncritical Loads Impedance Angle on the Tolerable Grid-side Voltage Fluctuations of Electric Spring
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Electric Springs can effectively mitigate the problems caused by network-side voltage instability by shifting the voltage fluctuations to non-critical loads. However, the "uncountable" input of non-critical loads in pursuit of voltage stabilization will inevitably bring new problems such as small fluctuations in grid-side voltage that the Electric Spring can withstand. In order to solve this problem, this paper takes the second-generation Electric Spring as the research object, explains its basic principle, analyzes its mechanism of regulating the voltage of critical loads, draws the phase diagram of the Electric Spring application configuration, and reveals the relationship between the critical load voltage and the Electric Spring voltage for different impedance angles of noncritical loads. The effect of different impedance angles of noncritical loads on the Electric Spring withstand voltage fluctuations on the grid side is discussed and defined with the help of MATLAB/Simulink tools, and the optimal configuration of different impedance angles of noncritical loads of the Electric Spring is derived and verified.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Comprehensive Evaluation Index of the Operation Point in the Interval Security Region Considering the Uncertainty of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Regional integrated energy system integrated with renewable energy sources will realize low-carbon, efficient, and sustainable utilization of energy, but it also faces more serious security challenges with the increasing penetration of renewable energy. The method of interval security region solves the problem of safety of operation points, but it is only limited to evaluating the operation points from the perspective of safety distance, without considering the differences in quantity and quality of operation points. Referring to the idea of ISR, this paper proposes the interval exergy efficiency function, interval energy supply efficiency function, and interval load margin function from the "quantity" and "quality" aspects of energy, and analyzes the distribution characteristics of the three functions through the case study. Among them, "quality" of energy refers to the high exergy efficiency of the system, which can fully convert low-quality energy and use high-quality energy; The "quantity" of energy includes two aspects, one is that the total energy supply is high within the maximum energy supply capacity of the system, and the other is that it has high load margin. This paper aims to enrich and improve the evaluation system of the operation points from multiple perspectives; and provide a theoretical basis for the follow-up study of the optimal control of the operation points.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Culture Conditions of the Chlorella sp Microalgae in a Photobioreactor for the Production of Biodiesel
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: In the present research work, the objective was to determine the appropriate conditions for the cultivation of the microalgae Chlorella sp in a Photobioreactor and to obtain the biomass of chlorella sp for biodiesel. For this, physical properties such as pH, temperature, CO2 flow and chemical properties such as the use of micronutrients and macronutrients in the growth medium of microalgae Chlorella sp were controlled. To obtain the biomass, centrifuge operations were carried out. drying it in an oven at a controlled temperature, extraction of the lipids by the soxhlet method using a solvent such as petroleum ether and then the lipid yield was determined, finally the transesterification synthesis reaction was carried out with methanol and KOH, obtaining biodiesel as a result. and glycerin this product was analyzed by infrared spectrophotometry (FTIR) which allowed identifying the composition of biodiesel as methyl oleate in greater proportion and others in small amounts.

articleTitle: Plasma-Assisted Nitrogen Doping of Ketjen Black to Promote Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction Reaction
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Nitrogen-doped carbon materials show promising prospects in enhancing the efficiency of cathodic oxygen reduction reactions. Compared to the traditional chemical methods, the dry processing by discharge plasma provides an efficient and eco-friendly modification method for higher catalyst activity. In this paper, we report on the morphology, structure, and elemental distribution of nitrogen-doped Ketjen Black which is modified by Ar/O2 surface dielectric barrier discharge at atmospheric pressure. Special attention is paid to the evaluation of oxygen reduction. Results show that the plasma can rapidly realize nitrogen doping in the process of forming new bonds. Additionally, oxygen reduction activity is enhanced by plasma etching via increasing the catalyst surface area and exposing more active sites. The doped nitrogen which appears as mainly graphitic N is more conducive to enhancing the activity of oxygen reduction reactions. This dry and efficient plasma method is expected to improve the reaction activity of the oxygen reduction catalyst in fuel cells.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Prediction of Market Fit for Electric Motor Products Based on QFD and Improved TOPSIS Method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: This study employs the Quality Function Deployment (QFD) method as a basis for evaluating and predicting the market applicability of three competitive electric motors, and employs a multi-criteria decision-making method to quantitatively evaluate and rank the three products. Specifically, the study uses Siemens, ABB and WEG electric motors as examples and proposes a product evaluation model based on QFD and an improved Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). User requirements are obtained through survey methods, and the weights of user requirements are calculated using an improved entropy weighting method. Then, the design requirements and design schemes are determined based on the QFD method. Finally, the TOPSIS method is improved to rank the product schemes and determine the final market applicability ranking. The experimental results and comparative studies demonstrate that the improved TOPSIS method overcomes the shortcomings of traditional methods, and verifies the efficiency, scientificity, and rationality of the product evaluation model based on QFD and improved TOPSIS.

articleTitle: Success and Failure of Electricity Market Deregulation in China and the Solutions: The Jiangsu Case
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: China’s electricity sector has undergone several rounds of reforms since 1985, with which significant changes have been made, including investment in new generation capacity, deregulation of generation capacity away from central government control, separation of government functions from enterprise management, restructuring of State Power Corporation and establishment of electricity markets. This paper provides a brief history of the archived and ongoing key policies for market reforms in China and Jiangsu Province. The market success and failure against this regime over the preceding half a decade are analyzed from a theoretical perspective, and policy implications are examined for understanding competition in markets based on new and upcoming power related policies. If these challenges or issues are not properly addressed, the potential positive impacts of the new reforms may be undermined. It is therefore recommended for China’s policy makers to strengthen the connection between renewable energy quota system (RQS), green electricity certificate and emission trading scheme (ETS), and improve the design of spot market and ancillary service market.

articleTitle: Lidar-VIO Based Mapping of Elevator Shaft with UAV for Verification of Spatial Dimensions
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Current methods utilized for the inspection of spatial dimensions of elevator shafts currently entail the need to take manual measurements at various levels of the shaft. Utilizing a UAV to collect spatial dimensions has potential to allow inspectors to complete their jobs in a safer manner and to boost the accuracy and consistency of inspection procedures. The study presented tests the feasibility of a designed UAV based system that hosts a miniaturized simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) scheme for usage of generating a point cloud of an elevator shaft environment for spatial dimension inspection. Secondary usages of the scheme are further demonstrated for cases where the scheme is employed while not mounted on a UAV. Average horizontal measurement accuracy for the system employed in flight is found to be 6.57 cm, and there is little difference in accuracy for mapping performed not in flight. Visual inertial odometry is investigated for pose estimation reliability in dark environments and environments with little structural information to process. Further sensor characterizations are performed to characterize properties of point clouds generated of a laboratory, a hallway, and an elevator shaft.

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting for Multiple Farms with Alternating Temporal and Graph Convolutional Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: Accurate wind power forecasting (WPF) is very important for stable and reliable power grid integration. Existing WPF approaches make predictions based on numerical weather prediction (NWP) of a single wind farm, where the spatial and temporal correlations among geographically adjacent wind farms are not considered. In this paper, we propose a novel WPF approach for multiple farms by integrating temporal convolution networks (TCN) and graph convolution networks (GCN). Abstracting the set of multiple wind farms into a graph, spatial information is aggregated with GCN on the irregular non-Euclidean mesh defined by the graph. For each farm, temporal information is fused via TCN. With alternating temporal and graph convolution layers, features are extracted from inputs and integrated for forecasting. As demonstrated by experimental results on data from a set of wind farms in Ningxia, China, the proposed WPF for multiple farms performs much better than existing approaches for a single farm.

articleTitle: Rapid Critical Eigenmodes Tracing via Inertia Equivalence in State Space
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The damping characteristics of critical electromechanical eigenmodes are varied with the power system conditions like the renewable energy fluctuations. However, the traditional eigenanalysis is difficult to trace the dynamic stability of high-order systems. Considering the variation of system parameters, we propose a rapid tracing method for the critical eigenmodes in this paper. For the tracing acceleration, the original state matrix order is reduced by inertia equivalence, and state variables are mapped to low-dimensional subspaces upon the generator clustering. When the cluster varies, a cluster variation index is proposed, and the classical QR method will be switched to guarantee the reliability of the traced critical eigenmodes. The comparison with the QR method verifies the effectiveness of the framework. Simulation tests demonstrate the accuracy and rapidity of the proposed method in critical eigenmode tracing.

articleTitle: ResNet-GRU Based Transient Voltage Stability Margin Evaluation of Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: The safe and stable operation of power system faces serious challenges such as the variability of operation mode and the lack of disturbance attenuation ability. To achieve the accurate voltage stability evaluation and provide reliable reference for emergency control, this paper proposes a transient voltage stability margin evaluation method based on deep residual network (ResNet) and gated recurrent unit (GRU). Firstly, a practical transient voltage stability margin index based on two-element table is presented to construct sample label in the case of large disturbances. Secondly, a ResNet-GRU hybrid model is established to quantitatively evaluate voltage stability margin. The complementary advantages of ResNet in spatial coupling feature extraction and GRU in temporal compliance relationship learning are fully exploited. Finally, case studies are performed in Northwest China local region power grid. A series of experiment and simulation results verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method for voltage stability margin evaluation.

articleTitle: Coordination Control of Wind Farm Combined with Energy Storage System for Frequency Control
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Green Energy (CEEGE)
abstract: To improve the frequency control of power systems with high penetration of renewable energy resources, this paper proposes a cooperation control method for the wind farm combined with energy storage for inertial support and primary frequency control. The whole station contains a multi-level control architecture based on the mixed hierarchical model predictive control technique that coordinates each unit to respond to frequency fluctuation. In the top layer, a linear model predictive control method is proposed to compute the respective active power reference of the whole energy station. To realize the coordination control of wind turbines, a nonlinear model predictive controller is designed to solve the issue of nonlinear character. The slack variable is introduced to the design of the cost function, which helps allocate the power reference among different turbines according to the maximum available energy and satisfies each unit's power constraint and stability constraint. For the coordination control of energy storage units, the slack variable is introduced to improve the efficiency of balancing states of charge among different units. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control structure and method, which decreases the frequency deviation to lower than 60% in the case study.
